objective: Connect normal project publication to shared canonical numerical preparation and independently owned source metadata without duplicating vector payloads.
contracts: Immutable project cache descriptor binds logical identity, authority and inventory; cached objects remain advisory and cannot certify Work.
Canonical raw vectors and projections have one project/scope store. Source-specific lexical/synapse/window metadata and routers retain separate namespaces and exact source heads.
Do not reconstruct full owner inventories or original bodies in directory lookup. Preserve read-only private overlays and never persist queries in shared source data.
Normal save queues preparation from its checked physical source while retaining the logical project scope. Track actual preparation readiness separately from source ACK.
Preparation and source publication may overlap; source writers remain independently owned. Shared canonical writer claims must not become the original publication gate.
A source router consumes only its own candidate keys; sharing a global matrix must not force source preparation to scan every other source's vectors.
An active source index claim or any live project owner prevents private shared cache reclamation.
No cold/missing derived data is treated as absent evidence. No top-K restriction on certification.
validation: Native source-layout ownership, same cache across owners, different projects/scopes separated, read-only behavior, corruption/mismatched descriptors and safe reclamation.
Normal hook/source save/background preparation/new-chat delivery and shared projection/router checks before expensive answering-model runs.
Real MiniLM numerical preparation where the installed dependency is available; distinguish deterministic storage tests from actual inference.
Retain resource guard: aggregate stop 3.5GiB, hard ceiling 4GiB, free disk >=2GiB. No subagents or new Python/Ruby implementation.
Current original-only matched paid comparison count stays 0/18 until the complete integration and fixed-runtime cohort gates pass.
